key_insight: A transferred monolayer graphene contact significantly improves AlInN/Si solar-cell performance by boosting current collection and fill factor without materially changing open-circuit voltage.
engineering_relevance: Graphene can serve as a low-temperature, semitransparent front contact to enhance nitride-based photovoltaic devices while preserving compatibility with Si-based substrates.
method: Grow AlxIn1-xN solar cells on p-type Si(100) with a thin amorphous-Si buffer layer
Study three Al compositions: x = 0.22, 0.35, and 0.43
Transfer a monolayer graphene film onto the front surface as the semitransparent conductive contact
evidence_signal: Devices with and without graphene were compared under illuminated and dark conditions, and graphene consistently improved short-circuit current density, fill factor, and overall power conversion efficiency across all three compositions.
watch_item: The graphene transfer step must be uniform and low-defect, since contact quality and scalability could strongly affect reproducibility and device-to-device variation.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
